ratings_why.fun: Every recruit phase is a real puzzle (who dies at the Source, who waits at B1, whose neighbours catch the Gift), and Bailiff, Kelt, Redd and the Hens chain in ways the builds don't list; a few plain stat cards keep it from 8.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because the board itself moves in a fight: a death at the head pulls the whole zigzag up a step, swapping rows, and a fish's slot is both its progress and its Spawn spot, which no auto-battler tribe does.

verdict_why: Nothing is broken and the rules now read; what is left is timing rulings and flavour polish, which would make it different rather than better.

points.text: Selling the Bailiff is an on-demand Spawn that stacks with Second-Run Hen, Jack and Mother Redd; say whether the leaving Bailiff still catches the Gift as the unit alongside.
Reunion Cock's 'exactly as many' clashes nicely with Pebble-Carrying Hen's +1 and Silver Smolt's Stamp, so tuning a year-class is a real choice; keep it, and show Stamps on the board.
Falls-Leaper only counts leaps for Attack; letting it also gain a Stamp or a permanent stat when the run cascades past it would tie it to the Long Road too.
Brother Grilse is the one T1 that ignores Stamps; a small Stamp hook (gains +1 Attack per Stamp when it leaps) would make him a seed for both builds.
Let Old Bradán resolve after every other Start of Combat effect, so Old Kelt's cascade sets the positions his replayed Gifts use; that turns the reading-order question into a combo.

standouts.why: Old Kelt turns one empty slot into a Stamp for the whole run and a sure homecoming, and costs a real slot decision.
The Bailiff stamps neighbours, blocks B1 for the Long Road, and when sold becomes a Spawn button; three jobs in one heron.
Mother Redd flips the tribe's cost: the same veteran comes home every fight and keeps paying Gifts, with Alevins for triples.

weakest.why: Falls-Leaper is a generic 'gains Attack when others move' card.
Brother Grilse does one obvious tempo job and reads no Stamps.
Claw-Marked Cock is a solid stat body; its row-swap trigger is cute but it feeds nothing else.

flags.note: With the Warden and Little Jack Gravel, Alevins to hand can make a golden and a Discover almost every turn.
Old Bradán's replayed Gifts add the tier, about twice the guide in fight; the designer already names the lever.
